Subject: Security exhibit clarification and evidence cadence

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA draft. Procurement and our security team reviewed the security exhibit and had a few items we'd like to clarify before legal redlines:

- SOC 2 evidence: can you confirm the cadence and what artifacts Redwood will provide versus what we need to pull from the portal? CareWell prefers quarterly evidence snapshots tied to specific assertions.
- Pen test language: the exhibit currently references a "periodic penetration test" without minimum frequency or advance notice. We need a defined window and notice period so our teams can plan.
- Audit rights: the current wording seems broad ("reasonable access to systems and logs"). Can we tighten this to scoped, scheduled inspections with a maximum of X days on-site or remote?

I've attached our annotated copy of the exhibit (CareWell_redlines_v1.pdf). We want to avoid a full MSA halt; our goal is to land on narrow, operational-friendly language.

Can we get your proposed positions and an operational runbook for evidence handoff? If possible, a short call this week would help.

Best,
Jorge

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit clarification and evidence cadence

Team — forwarding CareWell's ask. Quick summary of the asks and my initial thoughts:

1) SOC 2 evidence cadence: CareWell wants quarterly snapshots tied to assertions. We normally provide a quarterly summary (SOC 2 letter + evidence list) and can provide scoped artifacts on request; full artifact dumps are heavy. Suggest: we commit to quarterly assertion mapping + 10 artifact bundles/year (ad hoc requests) with a 10-business-day turnaround.

2) Pen test: they want defined windows and notice. Propose: annual external pen test for Redwood-managed infra, 30-day advance notice for a planned test, and 48-hour notice for emergency/forensic access when needed (with appropriate guardrails).

3) Audit rights: we need to push back on unlimited access. Propose: scoped audit rights limited to agreed assertions, one on-site or remote inspection per 12 months (with a vendor/scope list), plus access to redacted logs or synthetic snapshots for sensitive systems.

Action items: Karthik — can you draft legal positions for the exhibit (short bullets + suggested clause text)? Laura — can you sketch the operational evidence runbook (who owns the artifact bundles, where they live, typical turnaround)? I'll consolidate and send to CareWell with tracked redlines.

I've attached my annotated draft (redlines_track_changes.docx).

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Security & Assurance
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redlines_track_changes.docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security exhibit clarification and evidence cadence

Olga / Laura —

Below are the legal positions I recommend we push; draft clauses are inline. Keep these high level when we send to the customer, with the tracked doc attached for counsel review.

1) SOC 2 evidence:
- Position: Redwood will provide the SOC 2 report and an assertion-to-control mapping quarterly; supplemental artifacts will be provided on a reasonable, scoped basis subject to agreed SLAs.
- Suggested language (exhibit): "Provider shall deliver SOC 2 report and an assertion-control mapping on a quarterly basis. Provider will, upon Customer request, provide additional evidence reasonably necessary to verify controls, with Provider to respond within ten (10) business days to such requests. Requests requiring server-side or high-sensitivity artifacts may be subject to redaction or safe-harbor procedures described in the evidence-handbook.

2) Penetration testing
- Position: Defined cadence + guardrails on testing methods and data access.
- Suggested language: "Provider will perform a third-party penetration test at least once every 12 months. Customer may request a penetration test report; Provider will provide a redacted summary of findings. Penetration tests initiated by Customer require thirty (30) days advance notice and shall be scoped and scheduled through Provider's Security team.

3) Audit rights
- Position: Narrow, assertion-scoped audit rights; agree to one inspection per 12 months (on-site OR remote) and a mechanism for remediation and escalation.
- Suggested language: "Customer audit rights shall be limited to the controls and systems necessary to verify the assertions identified in the exhibit. Customer may perform one (1) inspection within any 12-month period, which may be conducted on-site or remotely. Provider will provide access to documentation, redacted logs, and system snapshots as agreed in the evidence-handbook.

I can turn these bullets into tracked text tonight. Also recommend we add a clause for confidentiality of redacted evidence and a requirement that Customer coordinate any external auditors through Provider to avoid uncontrolled data exfiltration.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -08:00

Adding ops detail for the evidence runbook. Quick notes to include in the customer-facing runbook:

- Ownership: Customer-facing evidence bundle curated by Customer Security (Olga) + runbook maintained in Redwood Confluence (link in exhibit).
- Cadence: Quarterly assertion snapshots delivered as PDF + a searchable S3 bucket of supporting redacted artifacts accessible via secure download links (pre-signed, 72-hour expiry).
- Turnaround: 10 business days for routine requests; escalated requests (legal / procurement) handled via security@redwood.com with a 5-business-day SLA and triage call within 48 hours.
- Pen test logistics: If Customer requests an on-demand pen test (beyond annual), require scheduling through security@redwood.com, proof of insurance for external testers, and a signed non-disclosure.

Suggested messaging for customer: keep commitments operational but avoid giving open-ended rights to raw logs or unlimited on-site access.

Laura

Head of Product Security Operations

Hi Jorge —

Thanks for the detailed feedback and for flagging the operational preferences. Per our internal review (legal + ops), attached is a consolidated set of proposed redlines that aim to narrow the audit scope while meeting CareWell's need for predictable evidence. Highlights:

- SOC 2: commit to quarterly SOC 2 report + assertion-control mapping; supplemental artifact requests handled within 10 business days; highly sensitive artifacts are provided redacted per the evidence-handbook.
- Pen test: annual third-party pen test for Redwood-managed infra; Customer-initiated tests require 30 days' notice and must be scheduled through Redwood Security. Emergency forensic access is available with 48-hour notice and a documented scope.
- Audit rights: limited to assertion-scoped verification; one inspection per 12-month period (on-site OR remote). Provider to offer redacted logs or snapshots as agreed in the evidence-handbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached tracked redlines (CareWell_SecExhibit_v3.pdf and redlines_track_changes.docx).
2) If the positions are acceptable, let's schedule a 30-minute alignment call this week to walk the redlines and a short runbook overview.
3) If we align on language, I'll ask Contracts to prepare an updated Order Form and a DocuSign for signature.

If helpful, here is a provisional DocuSign link to the updated exhibit for validation (non-binding until final review): https://www.docusign.net/validate?doc=CVW-117-sec-exhibit

Thanks — cc'ing Laura and Karthik for visibility.

Regards,
